records.quote: The two tangent - segments drawn to a circle from a point outside it are equal in length.
records.claim: Theorem 4: The two tangent segments drawn to a circle from a point outside it are equal in length.

records.quote: Given : A is a point outside the circle M
records.caption: Circle with centre M; external point A to the right; tangent segments AC (upper) and AB (lower) touching the circle at C and B; dashed lines MA, MC, MB.

records.quote: Given : A is a point outside the circle M, AB and AC are
records.text: Given: A is a point outside the circle M, AB and AC are two tangent segments of the circle at B and C. R.T.P: Prove that: AB = AC. onstruction: Draw MB, MC and MA.

records.quote: Proof : ∵ AB is a tangent segment to circle M
records.text: Proof: ∵ AB is a tangent segment to circle M ∴ m(∠ABM) = 90°. ∵ AC is a tangent segment to circle M ∴ m(∠ACM) = 90°.

records.quote: The two triangles ABM and ACM have :
records.text: The two triangles ABM and ACM have: m(∠B) = m(∠C) = 90° (Proof); MB = MC (Lengths of radii); AM is a common side. ∴ ΔABM ≡ ΔACM. We get: AB ≡ AC, ∴ AB = AC (Q.E.D.)
records.notes: Continues the proof from previous page.

records.claim: The straight line passing through the center of the circle and the intersection point of its two tangents bisects the angle between these two tangents. It also bisects the angle between the two radii passing through the two points of tangency.

Prove that: First: $\overrightarrow{AB}$ bisects $\angle DAX$. Second: $\overrightarrow{AD}\parallel\overrightarrow{XB}$.
solution: Given: $\overrightarrow{XA}$ and $\overrightarrow{XB}$ are two tangents to the circle, $m(\angle AXB)=70^\circ$ and $m(\angle DCB)=125^\circ$.
Proof: ∵ XA and XB are two tangent segments ∴ XA = XB

From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle XAB)=m(\angle DAB)=55^\circ$

records.label: Example
records.quote: M is an inscribed circle to the quadrilateral ABCD with radius
records.stem: In the opposite figure: M is an inscribed circle to the quadrilateral ABCD with radius length of 5 cm. AB = 9 cm and CD = 12 cm. Find the perimeter of ABCD, then calculate its area.
solution: ∵ The circle M is an inscribed circle to the quadrilateral ABCD
∴ The circle M touches the sides of ABCD at X, Y, Z and L
∵ $\overline{AX}$ and $\overline{AL}$ are two tangent segments to the circle M

records.quote: In the opposite figure :
records.caption: Quadrilateral ABCD with inscribed circle M (blue) touching AD at L, AB at X, CB at Y, CD at Z. Radius R drawn from M to Y. Dashed lines from M to vertices. Read from figure; verify.

records.label: Example
records.quote: are two tangent segments to circle M
solution: ∵ BX and BY are two tangent segments to circle M ∴ BX = BY
By addition, we get: (AX + BX) + (CZ + DZ) = AL + BY + CY + DL
∴ AB + CD = AD + BC = 1/2 the perimeter of ABCD
Area of ABCD = 1/2 AB × r + 1/2 BC × r + 1/2 CD × r + 1/2 AD × r
records.notes: Continuation of previous page's example; example number and stem not on this page. 'CZ= CY' then 'DZ = DL' as printed (CZ = CY pairs with DZ = DL on the right); printed AL, DL labels as read.

objectives.label: Relate tangents at chord ends and tangent segments
objectives.description: Describe tangents at the ends of a diameter or chord, and identify tangent segments and the chord of tangency.

objectives.label: Prove and use that tangent segments from an outside point are equal
objectives.description: Prove Theorem 4 using congruent triangles and use it to find unknown lengths and angles.

objectives.label: Use the symmetry corollaries of two tangents
objectives.description: Use the fact that the line through the centre and the tangents' intersection is the axis of the chord of tangency and bisects the angles at A and M.

objectives.label: Work with a circle inscribed in a polygon
objectives.description: Recognise an inscribed circle and use equal tangent segments to find perimeter, area and side lengths.

objectives.label: Apply properties of common tangents of two circles
objectives.description: Distinguish internal and external common tangents and show their segments are equal; compute their lengths.
